scenes.title: Read the amendment working-copy warning
scenes.narration_exact: The editor identifies the same Training record and displays an important notice: an amendment is in progress, and the last finalized revision remains authoritative until the amendment is finalized. Read that distinction before editing. Station slash group, External ID, dates, Course, Course code, Location and Narrative are shown here. Opening this editor has not, by itself, replaced the finalized version with a newly signed correction.

scenes.title: Make the specific field correction
scenes.narration_exact: Edit only the field that needs correction. Here, Course code changes from Academy, R E C, twenty-nine, to Academy, R E C, twenty-nine A. The Course title, fictional workspace and software-only narrative remain unchanged. A focused correction is easier to review later than an unexplained rewrite of unrelated details. Check the new field value and the amendment notice before moving to the save controls.

scenes.title: Save the correction as a working draft
scenes.narration_exact: At the bottom of the editor, review Reason code, Reason and the available save actions. This example uses Training Correction as its reason code. The attestation is still unchecked. Choose Save draft to retain the working correction without finalizing it. Save and finalize is a separate action. The complete reason and attestation will be reviewed again in the finalization panel before the amendment is signed.

Keep the row number and transition together so you open the version you actually intend to inspect.

scenes.title: Keep corrections understandable across departments
scenes.narration_exact: The same careful correction and revision checks can support authorized documentation in community paramedicine or mental health response teams, search-and-rescue organizations, security companies, wildland contractors and industrial emergency teams, as well as Fire and EMS departments. Use a specific reason, keep the attestation truthful and inspect the saved result. A working draft, a finalized amendment, a comparison and an earlier revision each serve a different purpose when explaining what a record said and how it changed.
